text: The guy next to you on the train lets out a monster sneeze.

text: Someone asks: 'Is it just me?'
note: Confirms a shared problem. Relief for whoever asked.

text: A friend asks: 'Can you fix my laptop?'
note: Accepts without committing to success. Very sensible.

text: Someone says: 'I think I deleted it.'
note: Practical first step. British for trash folder.

text: A colleague says: 'It works on my machine.'
note: Deduction in four words. The classic reply.

text: Someone asks: 'What's the wifi?'
sample: It's on the router, hang on.
note: Buys a moment while you go and look.

text: Someone says: 'My phone's at two percent.'
note: Urgent and funny. Perfect for a dying battery.

text: A colleague asks: 'Did you get my email?'
note: Honest status plus an action. Two beats, no excuses.

text: Someone says: 'It's asking for a code.'
note: Future “will” for deduction. Very natural and common.

text: Someone says: 'I've been hacked!'
sample: Change the password now, then talk.
note: Prioritises the action over the conversation. Exactly right.

text: A colleague asks: 'Can you hear me?'
note: Adverb plus “yeah”. The quickest confirmation on a call.

text: Someone says: 'This app is useless.'
note: Turns a complaint into a diagnosis in three words.

text: Someone says: 'I don't understand any of this.'
sample: You don't need to — just click that.
note: Removes the pressure to understand. Kind and effective.

text: A colleague says: 'I've pushed the fix.'
note: Immediate reciprocal action. Standard developer exchange.

text: Someone asks: 'Is it safe to click this?'
note: Caution stated as a helpful step. Never just say no.

text: Someone says: 'The printer's not working.'
note: Three words of universal truth. Always gets a laugh.

text: A friend says: 'Which laptop should I buy?'
sample: What are you using it for?
chunk: what are you using it for?
note: The only correct first question. Prevents bad advice.

text: Someone says: 'I've got no signal.'
note: Practical suggestion in five words.

text: A colleague says: 'Sorry, my connection's terrible.'
sample: You keep cutting out — type it?
note: Offers a fallback channel. Saves the whole conversation.

text: Someone says: 'Can you screenshot that?'
note: Present continuous as instant compliance.

text: Someone says: 'It's spinning and nothing's happening.'
note: Patience as advice. Correct surprisingly often.

text: A colleague asks: 'Who owns this service?'
note: Relative clause delivering the verdict. Very efficient.

text: Someone says: 'I fixed it!'
note: The question that prevents the same bug next week.

text: Someone asks: 'Are you free Friday?'
note: Soft yes that leaves room. Extremely common.

text: Someone says: 'Shall we say eight?'
note: Bare confirmation. Nothing more is needed.

text: Someone says: 'Sorry, I'm going to be late.'
note: Removes the guilt instantly. Very modern and warm.

text: Someone asks: 'Does Thursday suit you?'
note: Fixed phrase for agreement. Always with “by”.

text: Someone says: 'I'll have to cancel, sorry.'
note: Forgives without any fuss. Keeps the friendship easy.

text: Someone asks: 'What time works for you?'
note: Total flexibility in three words. Very generous.

text: Someone says: 'Still on for tonight?'
note: Confirms twice in one line. Removes all doubt.

text: Someone asks: 'Can we make it half an hour later?'
note: Agreement with emphasis. Warmer than a plain yes.

text: Someone says: 'I completely forgot.'
note: Normalises the mistake. Ends the apology.

text: Someone asks: 'Where shall we meet?'
note: Offers both sides of town in four words. Very natural.

text: Someone says: 'I'm outside.'
note: Present continuous as immediate action. Perfect for arrival.

text: Someone asks: 'Do you want to come?'
note: Enthusiastic yes with a joke. Very warm.

text: Someone says: 'Let's play it by ear.'
note: Accepts vagueness but pins one detail. Quietly practical.

text: Someone asks: 'Are we booking or just turning up?'
sample: Just turning up, it'll be quiet.
note: Answers and justifies in four words.

text: Someone says: 'Sorry, my diary's a mess.'
note: Solidarity plus a solution. Ends the negotiation.

text: Someone asks: 'Same time next week?'
note: Fixed pair. Confirms a recurring plan warmly.

text: Someone says: 'I might be a bit late.'
note: Removes the deadline entirely. Extremely kind.

text: Someone asks: 'Have you got plans tonight?'
note: Flattering non-answer. Signals they take priority.

text: Someone says: 'That's the weekend sorted then.'
note: Standard enthusiasm. Note the “to” before a gerund or noun.

text: Someone asks: 'Shall I book it?'
note: Delegates and appreciates in four words.

text: Someone says: 'I'll pick you up at six.'
note: Confirms your side of the arrangement. Small but important.

text: Someone asks: 'How long are you staying?'
note: Vague and honest. “Probably” protects you.

text: Someone says: 'We should do this more often.'
note: Affectionate joke that both agrees and teases.

text: Someone asks: 'Is it a late one?'
note: Declines the late night while sounding regretful.

text: Someone says: 'See you Saturday!'
sample: See you then — don't be late.
note: Warm closing tease. Only for people you know well.
